biography: Pedro Hiltbrand's journey began amidst the sun-drenched karting tracks of Valencia, Spain. Born into a family with gasoline flowing through their veins, Pedro received his first kart at the tender age of six. While other children were playing football, Pedro was mastering the art of apexes and slip angles. His aggressive style, honed through countless hours battling wheel-to-wheel with local rivals, quickly caught the eye of talent scouts. A defining moment came at the Spanish Karting Championship in 2016, where, after starting last due to a mechanical issue, he clawed his way to victory, showcasing a raw determination that became his trademark. Now at 25, Pedro is making the difficult transition from Kart 2-Stroke 125cc Shifter to single-seater racing, looking to leave his mark in the higher echelons of motorsport.
drivingStyle: Pedro's driving style is characterized by an unapologetic aggression. He's a late-braking specialist, often diving into corners with a ferocity that borders on recklessness. While this approach can lead to spectacular overtakes, it also results in occasional lock-ups and tire degradation. Tire management isn't exactly his forte, but he compensates with sheer pace and unwavering determination. Under pressure, Pedro thrives, often delivering his best performances when the stakes are highest.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from a controversial collision in the 2018 Karting World Championship final. Pedro accuses Bellini of deliberately taking him out.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky undershirt, regardless of the weather.
Listens to a specific Spanish flamenco song before every race to calm his nerves.
Refuses to walk under ladders and always throws a pinch of salt over his left shoulder if he spills any.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about playing it safe; it's about pushing the limits. If you're not on the edge, you're taking up too much space."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2016 Spanish Karting Championship after starting last due to mechanical failure, a testament to his never-give-up attitude.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2019 European Karting Championship, costing him a potential title win.
